To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the GOME- 2 tropospheric columns show good agreement with ground-based measurements, and that the random error is approximately 0.
GOME-2 total NO2 columns can be retrieved with an estimated random uncertainty of 0.45–0.5 × (10 15 molec cm−2) and a systematic uncertainty of 0–0.1 × 1015 (molec cm−2).
The GOME-1 and GOME-1/ERS-2 data sets are the best available data sets of global NO2 columns for the 1996 to 2003 time period.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the retrieval of total and stratospheric NO 2 column from satellite data, and tropospheric column from satellite and ground-based data.
the development of a fast and robust algorithm for the retrieval of total and stratospheric and tropospheric columns of NO2 from GOME- 2 data.
the operational retrieval of NO2 columns from GOME2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GOME-2 is a very good successor of GOME, with the advantage of a higher sensitivity to tropospheric NOx and a much better stability of the instrument.
the GOME- 2 NO2 tropospheric columns can be considered operationally ready for use in the O3M-SAF products.
the GOME-3 NO2 retrieval is an improvement over GOME-2 in terms of the systematic error and that the random errors in both GOME-2 and GOME-3 are comparable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GOME-2 provides an excellent opportunity to monitor the NO2 troposphere on a global scale.
the operational GOME-2 total and troposphered NO2 column products are of high quality.
the GOME- 2 NO2 slants and total columns are of high accuracy and the tropospheric columns of good accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GOME-1 and GOME-3 instruments have been designed with an improved quartz diffuser, which has a significant impact on the systematic error in NO2 slant column retrievals.
the operational retrieval of tropospheric NOx columns from GOME is feasible, with a precision of about 0.8× 10 15 molec cm−2 and an uncertainty of about 40–80 % for polluted conditions.

the operational GOME-2 total and troposphered NO2 columns are of high quality, and can be used for the validation of other space-borne instruments such as the Ozone Monitoring Instrument (OMI) on the Aura and Metop platforms.
